items.label: f02-key-reuse-changed-details
items.front: A reserve command reuses a stored requestKey but with a different month. What does replay do?
items.back: It throws 'Request key was already used with different reservation details.' because the fingerprint (cycle plus quote facts) no longer matches.

items.label: f01-whole-workspace-cc
items.front: Record version fields exist on items, plans and subscribers. Why do two operators editing unrelated records still conflict?
items.back: commit compares the whole raw stored string with the tab's baseline before reduce; any accepted write changes those bytes, so concurrency control is whole-workspace, not per-record.

items.label: f03-cancel-is-terminal
items.front: What stops a cancelled shipment from returning its stock a second time?
items.back: Cancelled has no allowed transitions, so any further transition fails the transitions-table check before the stock-returning branch can run.

items.label: f04-server-commit-five-steps
items.front: Name the five steps of commit that a server version must keep, and which two move into the database.
items.back: Lock, replay check, base comparison, reduce, write. The lock and the base comparison move into the database (transaction / conditional update).

items.prompt: An item matches three of a subscriber's preferred tags but also carries one of their blocked tags. Where does it appear in recommendations?

choices.text: At the bottom, because each blocked tag subtracts points from the score
Nowhere: excluded tags are a hard eligibility filter applied before any scoring
Near the top, because three preferred matches outweigh one blocked-tag penalty
In the middle, because blocked tags only halve the rating component

choices: At the bottom, because each blocked tag subtracts points from the score
Nowhere: excluded tags are a hard eligibility filter applied before any scoring
Near the top, because three preferred matches outweigh one blocked-tag penalty
In the middle, because blocked tags only halve the rating component

items.explanation: eligible() requires active, in stock and no blocked tag; recommendations filters on eligible before computing scores.

items.prompt: Two tabs race to reserve the last unit of an item from the same base. Which check rejects the loser, and what is the consequence for unrelated edits?

choices.text: Web Locks reject the second tab outright; it never reads storage
replay rejects it because both tabs used the same request key
The raw-baseline comparison inside the lock rejects it before reduce looks at stock, so any two concurrent writes conflict even on unrelated records
reduce's stock check rejects it with an out-of-stock error; unrelated records never conflict

choices: Web Locks reject the second tab outright; it never reads storage
replay rejects it because both tabs used the same request key
The raw-baseline comparison inside the lock rejects it before reduce looks at stock, so any two concurrent writes conflict even on unrelated records
reduce's stock check rejects it with an out-of-stock error; unrelated records never conflict

items.explanation: Inside the lock the winner has already replaced the stored bytes, so current.raw !== base.raw throws first. Safe, but coarse.

items.prompt: Of the two fixes proposed for non-replayable transitions, why does the guide prefer making transitions replayable in the model over a UI reload-and-check?

choices.text: It keeps the guarantee in the tested domain layer, using version expected+1 and the last history entry as the transition's natural fingerprint
The model fix needs a new requestKey field on every transition command, which makes it more explicit
The UI fix cannot be implemented because React cannot reload storage
The UI fix is preferred; the model fix would break reservation replay

choices: It keeps the guarantee in the tested domain layer, using version expected+1 and the last history entry as the transition's natural fingerprint
The model fix needs a new requestKey field on every transition command, which makes it more explicit
The UI fix cannot be implemented because React cannot reload storage
The UI fix is preferred; the model fix would break reservation replay

items.explanation: No new field is needed: matching version and last history entry identify the already-applied transition. The codebase puts every other guarantee in the domain layer.

items.prompt: Porting to SQL, a teammate proposes: SELECT for an existing shipment for (subscriber, month); if none, INSERT. Why is that insufficient?

choices.text: Two concurrent requests can both see no row and both insert; only unique constraints with transaction handling can arbitrate concurrent inserts
SQL cannot store request keys, so idempotency must stay in the browser
It is sufficient as long as the SELECT and INSERT run in the same HTTP request handler
SELECT is too slow; an index on subscriber alone would fix the problem

choices: Two concurrent requests can both see no row and both insert; only unique constraints with transaction handling can arbitrate concurrent inserts
SQL cannot store request keys, so idempotency must stay in the browser
It is sufficient as long as the SELECT and INSERT run in the same HTTP request handler
SELECT is too slow; an index on subscriber alone would fix the problem

items.explanation: A preliminary lookup by itself cannot arbitrate concurrent inserts.

items.prompt: A subscriber's May box was cancelled. The operator starts a fresh reservation for the same subscriber and May with a brand-new request key. What happens and which rule decides it?

choices.text: It succeeds, because a new request key is a new attempt and the old shipment is cancelled
It succeeds only if the fingerprint matches the cancelled shipment's quote
It is refused by the subscriber-month cycle constraint, a business rule that holds even after cancellation and is separate from request-key idempotency
It returns the cancelled shipment, because replay matches on subscriber and month

choices: It succeeds, because a new request key is a new attempt and the old shipment is cancelled
It succeeds only if the fingerprint matches the cancelled shipment's quote
It is refused by the subscriber-month cycle constraint, a business rule that holds even after cancellation and is separate from request-key idempotency
It returns the cancelled shipment, because replay matches on subscriber and month

items.explanation: Idempotency handles transport uncertainty; the cycle constraint enforces business policy. reduce throws 'already has a reservation, including cancelled history'.

items.prompt: You add 'retail cannot be below cost' to validateItem. Besides one existing test fixture, what else does this rule change that belongs in the PR description?

choices.text: Nothing else: validateItem only runs when the item editor form is submitted
Recommendations start excluding below-cost items from scoring
Existing shipments are re-priced to retail when the rule is added
Backup imports: validateState calls validateItem, so an old backup containing a below-cost item will now be rejected

choices: Nothing else: validateItem only runs when the item editor form is submitted
Recommendations start excluding below-cost items from scoring
Existing shipments are re-priced to retail when the rule is added
Backup imports: validateState calls validateItem, so an old backup containing a below-cost item will now be rejected

items.explanation: The rule applies to every backup on import because validateState calls validateItem.

items.prompt: A Packed transition is written to storage but its acknowledgement is lost; the operator retries from the same snapshot. What do they see, and why?

choices.text: A misleading 'Workspace changed in another tab' error, because replay only short-circuits reserve commands, so the retry falls through to the stale-baseline check
The shipment moves to Packed twice and its history gets a duplicate entry
A 'transition is not allowed' error, because Packed to Packed is not in the table
Success, because every command type is replayed by request key

choices: A misleading 'Workspace changed in another tab' error, because replay only short-circuits reserve commands, so the retry falls through to the stale-baseline check
The shipment moves to Packed twice and its history gets a duplicate entry
A 'transition is not allowed' error, because Packed to Packed is not in the table
Success, because every command type is replayed by request key

items.explanation: replay returns early unless c.type === 'reserve'; the write landed, so the stored bytes differ from the old base.

items.prompt: A box reservation selects five items and the fifth is out of stock. What must the accepted state look like afterwards, and why not just clamp the fifth item's stock at zero?

choices.text: The first four items are decremented and the shipment is saved as partial, which is honest about what was available
The fifth item is set to zero and the shipment is saved, since clamping keeps stock non-negative
The first four decrements are kept but the shipment is dropped, to be reconciled by a later stocktake
Completely unchanged, because the reducer works on a clone; clamping would hide overselling instead of proving the reservation was possible

choices: The first four items are decremented and the shipment is saved as partial, which is honest about what was available
The fifth item is set to zero and the shipment is saved, since clamping keeps stock non-negative
The first four decrements are kept but the shipment is dropped, to be reconciled by a later stocktake
Completely unchanged, because the reducer works on a clone; clamping would hide overselling instead of proving the reservation was possible

items.explanation: The guide: if the fifth selected item is unavailable, the first four items in the accepted state must remain untouched; tests compare accepted bytes before and after rejection.

items.prompt: Adding a 'skip this month' option: what is the critical race, and what prevents both sides from succeeding?

choices.text: A skip racing a catalog edit; per-item versions prevent it
One client skipping while another reserves the same month; both must go through one authoritative subscriber-month slot with a transaction or uniqueness design
Two skips of the same month; a disabled skip button after the first click prevents it
There is no race, because skips do not touch stock

choices: A skip racing a catalog edit; per-item versions prevent it
One client skipping while another reserves the same month; both must go through one authoritative subscriber-month slot with a transaction or uniqueness design
Two skips of the same month; a disabled skip button after the first click prevents it
There is no race, because skips do not touch stock

items.explanation: If each checks a separate table without an appropriate transaction or uniqueness design, both could succeed.

items.prompt: An item starts with stock 4. A box containing it is reserved, packed, then cancelled. What is its stock now, and could a second cancellation change it?

choices.text: 2: reserve and pack each subtract one, and cancel returns only the reserved unit
4: reserve subtracts one, packing changes nothing, cancel returns one, and Cancelled is terminal so no second return is possible
3: cancellation after packing does not return stock because the unit is assumed boxed
4 now, but a second cancel would raise it to 5 because cancel always increments

choices: 2: reserve and pack each subtract one, and cancel returns only the reserved unit
4: reserve subtracts one, packing changes nothing, cancel returns one, and Cancelled is terminal so no second return is possible
3: cancellation after packing does not return stock because the unit is assumed boxed
4 now, but a second cancel would raise it to 5 because cancel always increments

items.explanation: stock means units available for new reservations; packing does not subtract again; cancellation from Reserved or Packed returns one per item and is terminal (transitions.Cancelled is empty).

items.prompt: You add a stock-movement ledger. Why can't the sum of movements alone explain the current stock of the seed items?

choices.text: It can: the seed data is generated from movements at startup
Because cancellations are not recorded as movements
Seed stock existed before any movement was recorded, so you need an opening balance (or accepted stocktake events) as the reconciliation baseline
Because movements are stored as floats and drift over time

Because cancellations are not recorded as movements
Seed stock existed before any movement was recorded, so you need an opening balance (or accepted stocktake events) as the reconciliation baseline
Because movements are stored as floats and drift over time

items.explanation: Movement totals alone cannot explain existing sample stock unless there is an opening balance.

items.prompt: A plan used by last month's shipments is archived. Why must historical validation NOT check whether the plan is currently available?

choices.text: Because historical shipments are never validated at all after acceptance
It must check it; an archived plan means the old shipment should be flagged invalid
Because archived plans are deleted, so there is nothing to check against
Historical validation checks internal receipt consistency and references; checking today's availability would make old records unreadable just because the plan was archived

choices: Because historical shipments are never validated at all after acceptance
It must check it; an archived plan means the old shipment should be flagged invalid
Because archived plans are deleted, so there is nothing to check against
Historical validation checks internal receipt consistency and references; checking today's availability would make old records unreadable just because the plan was archived

items.explanation: New reservations evaluate current eligibility; historical records are judged on their own accepted facts.
